scope: Proposition 4.11 (Intermediate regularity and pole control) of the manuscript “Global Support and Convex Injectivity Domains under Weak MTW” (preprints/Global-Support-and-Convex-Injectivity-Domains-under-Weak-MTW-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 360 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e16087753fc93a84), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 18. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. statement: Let (u, v) be a dual pair and 0 < t < 1. Then Qtu = −Q1−tv ∈ C1,1 (M). (4.13) The C1,1 seminorm is bounded solely in terms of M, g, t. If (xt(z), pt(z)) = F−1 t (z) and Φs denotes geodesic flow on TM, then (xt(z), pt(z)) = Φ−t(z, grad Qtu(z)), xt(z) = expz(−t grad Qtu(z)). (4.14) In particular the pole and momentum are Lipschitz, with constants depending only on M, g, t. There are also rt, bt > 0, depending only on M, g, t, such that every projected pair z = expx(tp) satisfies u(x′ ) + ct(x′ , z) ≥ u(x) + ct(x, z) + btd(x, x′ )2 if d(x, x′ ) < rt. (4.15) These assertions use no density hypothesis. On every compact subinterval of (0, 1), their constants can be chosen uniformly.
